terms.gloss: before one’s eyes, under one’s very nose
evidence: Verg. A. 1.114: ante oculōs pontus in puppim ferit (Lewis & Short s.v. ante)
Cic. Fam. 14.2.3: nam mihi ante oculōs diēs noctēsque versāris
Traupman 104: under one’s very nose, ante oculōs
terms.comment: Latin puts it before the eyes, not under the nose; the person is in the genitive or understood: ante oculōs tuōs, right in front of you.

phrases.latin: nam mihi ante oculōs diēs noctēsque versāris
phrases.english: for you are before my eyes day and night

sources: Lewis & Short: ante · Lewis & Short: oculus
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 104.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
